_meta.source: Illustrative keeper-vs-ablation-twin comparison. Mechanism mirrors ScenarioConfig.as_zero_forcing_ablation (src/market_sim/config/scenarios.py) and the D-2 mechanism registry (src/market_sim/data/floor_mechanisms.py): the twin re-solves the keeper's exact config with every merchant floor/bridge/drag/haircut off, structural must-run kept (nuclear must-run, CHP steam-following, coal take-or-pay, import boundaries). Proportions are faithful to typical keeper behaviour but this is NOT raw solver output and describes no registered run.
_meta.description: Per-class annual energy (TWh), keeper vs zero-forcing ablation twin, for the results-calibration ablation-twin narrative. delta_twh = keeper - ablation: the energy each class's floors 'buy'. Classes with structural-only support (nuclear, coal take-or-pay) show near-zero deltas; merchant-floored classes (ST gas, CT peakers) show the floors' contribution; the flexible margin (gas-CC) absorbs the offset with a negative delta.

run_metadata.note: Annual-average TWh across the three bundle years.

classes.note: Structural must-run - kept in the twin by definition; a nonzero delta here would be a coverage bug (assert_ablation_coverage).
The flexible margin: with merchant floors off, CC picks up the energy the floors had forced onto ST gas and CT peakers.
Coal take-or-pay is structural and stays on in the twin; the small residual delta is the merchant committed-tranche floor.
Largest floor-bought energy: the RMR/reliability commitment floors carry most of this class's dispatch.
Reserve/AS-driven commitment floors; the class the 15% forced-energy budget (C8) watches most closely.
Below the 2%-of-load materiality floor - reported by the D-1/D-2 diagnostics but never gated.

totals.note: System totals nearly conserve (demand is fixed); floors mostly reallocate energy between classes rather than add it. The small net delta is absorbed by imports/storage losses not shown.
